title: AWS WAF and Shield
description: Protect web applications with WAF rules and defend against DDoS attacks with AWS Shield.

data.text: AWS WAF (Web Application Firewall) and AWS Shield protect your web applications from common attacks and distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks. WAF filters malicious requests at the application layer, while Shield provides DDoS protection at the network and transport layers.

AWS WAF lets you monitor HTTP and HTTPS requests that come to CloudFront distributions, API Gateway APIs, AppSync GraphQL APIs, and Application Load Balancers. You define **rules** that identify malicious requests and tell WAF what to do with them — allow, block, or count.

data.title: WAF Rule Types
items: **IP set** — Allow or block requests from specific IP addresses or ranges
**String match** — Match specific strings in headers, query strings, or body
**SQL injection** — Block requests containing SQL injection patterns
**Cross-site scripting (XSS)** — Block requests containing XSS patterns
**Size constraint** — Block requests with unusually large components
**Rate-based rule** — Block IPs that exceed a request threshold

data.text: **AWS Shield Standard** is automatically enabled for all AWS customers at no cost. It protects against common network and transport layer DDoS attacks. **AWS Shield Advanced** provides enhanced protection, cost protection, and access to the DDoS Response Team (DRT). Shield Advanced integrates with WAF and Route 53 for a comprehensive DDoS defense.

cards.title: Shield Advanced
cards.description: Paid enhanced protection for critical applications.

data.text: WAF protects against application-layer attacks (Layer 7). For network-layer DDoS protection, you need Shield Advanced. Use both for comprehensive protection.

points: WAF filters HTTP/HTTPS requests using rules for IP, patterns, and rate limits
Web ACLs are collections of rules attached to CloudFront, API Gateway, or ALB
Shield Standard provides free DDoS protection; Shield Advanced adds cost protection and DRT access
Rate-based rules automatically block IPs that exceed request thresholds
data.takeaway: WAF and Shield work together to protect your applications. Start with WAF managed rule groups and Shield Standard, then evaluate Shield Advanced for critical workloads.
